result.text: We are up to chapter nine, פרק ט. This is the last chapter of the introductory nine chapters. of this chapter is kind of a contrast to what we explained in the previous two chapters. The previous two chapters we explained the concept of making a יחוד of seeing how everything is united and all of the stages in the סדר השתלשלות from the top to the bottom are really interconnected and function it and function as a single unit, so we shouldn't see it as a bunch of separate stages. This chapter is going to explain the importance of understanding how each stage comes through a צמצום, and therefore we sh- these even though there are all these changes and all this diversity within the סדר השתלשלות, but compared to the essence before the צמצום, there's no real change. And so, that's going to be the other fundamental idea when we're learning the entire ספר is at every stage to understand the צמצום and be able to kind of see past that to see the fallacy of that and how it's really just from our perspective, but there's a deeper perspective from which there is not a change. Okay, let's jump in. אך הנה לכאורה אינו מובן, seemingly we have a question, something is not understood, מה שאמר אני הוי' לא שניתי. The verse that it says and it's very often quoted throughout קבלה and חסידות that it says, "I am God, I have not changed." And this is a פסוק in מלאכי where God is talking to the Jewish people and the simple explanation according to רש״י actually fits very nicely with what we're explaining here. And this is the idea that Hashem is telling the Jewish people that even when I'm patient with you and I don't seem to punish the wicked, that doesn't mean that my uh in my like inner preferences, so to speak, have changed. That God still, you know, doesn't want evil and wants righteousness, and even if he's not exacting punishment or whatever it is, but he hasn't changed his fundamental position. And this idea is brought, this verse is brought, in general, to represent this idea that God is eternal, and he is beyond changing, he's not affected by what happens in our world, and um he's always, you know, staying constant, always staying the same. שזה מדבר במלכות דאין סוף עצמו which this, when it says "אני", like we said before, "אני" represents מלכות, and here we're talking about מלכות of אין סוף itself. In other words, God's essential self-expression does not change. But we have a question based on what we explained in the past two chapters, הרי אם בבחינת מלכות דעשיה יש בו שינוי בין דין לחסד, שהוא בבחינת התפעלות וכולי. If we witness that in the way that מלכות of עשיה is which is the way God expressed himself in the physical world and like we said that's connected all the way back up to מלכות of אין סוף, and so really they're functioning as a single unit, and yet we see that there are changes happening on the level of מלכות of עשיה and there is this idea of a change from let's say judgment to kindness and things like that, which is the idea of התפעלות, of being um having like a reaction to what our we're doing, and if we act a certain way, things are going to go this way, if we act differently, then we'll get a different response. So that seems to be this idea of התפעלות, of a reaction. And like we said, everything is connected. So מוכרח שגם במלכות דאין סוף יש שינוי זה, so then, seemingly, there must be this same corresponding change happening all the way back up to מלכות of אין סוף that at that highest level, God seems to be responding and reacting to what we're doing and and changing in a way. Second of all, just the very act of creating the world with such diversity and changing every day seems to be a constant change. And third of all, how could it be that when we pray, we actually ask God to change his mind? We say, אנו אומרים, we say יהי רצון מלפניך, may it be the will before you. In other words, we're asking for רצון חדש, for him to have a new will, to change his mind, שיתהפך רצון של דין לחסד, to change a desire of judgment to one of kindness. You know, repeal that and rip it up and give us a good, you know, wonderful decree. ואנו רואים, and we see שינויים רבים בכל עת ושעה וכולי, and we see that there's constantly changes every every day, every moment. כל אשר חפץ עשה תמיד בשמים ובארץ וכולי, like it says in תהלים, that whatever God desires he does in heavens and the earth. And you know, again, if everything is coming from God's will, God's desire, so then the world is constantly changing, how are these not a change in God? So that's the question with a few different angles, a few different nuances, but in general, how can we say if everything is united and there's no intermediaries, God forbid, or anything like that, and it's God directly choosing and creating everything that's happening, how can we say that he is not changing, right? So like the philosophers, like Aristotle or some of these other types of things, they sought to remove God, because of this question, from the picture, and say, "Well, you know, he's really just this like abstract force that's beyond everything, and everything that's going on in creation is just through angels or lower forces that he creates." But we don't say that, we say that those are all a facade, that really it's just him. So how do we answer this question? והתירוץ לכל זה הוא ענין הצמצום, כידוע. And so the general answer to this is the idea of the צמצום. We're going to explain the idea of the צמצום in more depth and more length in chapters 12 and 13, so we'll get there. And throughout the entire book actually, this is going to be a recurring theme at each stage to understand the צמצום at that stage. And that's what he's going to explain now, that in order to see God's unity properly, we want to see how God is connected to what's going on down here in the world, and so what happens reflects on his essence, but we also want to recognize that he's not changing, he's not getting lowered by that, and his essence remains beyond all of this. And this is through appreciating the idea of the צמצום. כידוע, as is known, דאם היה השפע דרך עילה ועלול, היה נופל ענין שינוי והתפעלות וכולי, that if God were conducting the world in a process of cause and effect where there was a direct direct connection or relationship between God and what he's creating, so then it would be accurate to describe it with God changing and having this kind of reaction. אבל מאחר ש ההמשכה בבחינת אור וזיו לבד, but since God is only creating the world with what's described as metaphorically like a light or a ray, and we'll talk more about that, וגם הוא על ידי צמצום, and even that light and ray is not coming directly from Him, but only through a צמצום, על כן אין בעצמות אלוקות שום שינוי כלל. So in the essence of God, there's no real change. It's always the same, and it's just the way it's being revealed to us, way it appears to us, is what changes. גם במלכות דמלכות דעשיה, even all the way down to the level of מלכות דמלכות דעשיה, that the essential Godliness that's there that's driving that is staying the same, and it's just the way that it's expressed that's changing. וכן הוא עד רום המעלות, and that's true all the way up to the highest levels. ואחר, that at each stage, all the the appearance of changes and diversity that's happening with סדר השתלשלות is only happening because the צמצום gives that appearance, but the essence of what's going on there is not changing. ואחר הצמצום יש בחינת שינוי, but after the צמצום, there are changes, and in other words, God does create this reality for us where we live in, where there there are these changes, there is this diversity, and that's where we live in after the צמצום, but there's also, parallel to that, at the same time, this deeper fundamental level where things are not changing. וזהו מצד המקבלים לבד כידוע, and this level where things are changing is only from the perspective of the recipients, which is us and all of creation, but not from God's higher perspective.
